title: Directional telecom photons from a chirally coupled quantum dot
authors: Kristina Bodiroga, Jacob Ewaniuk, Andrew N. Wakileh, Lucas Rantz, Ivanna M. Boras Vazquez, Dan Dalacu, Phillip J. Poole, Robin L. Williams, Xiao-Liu Chu, Nir Rotenberg
abstract: Chiral quantum light-matter interfaces, where the internal spin state of a quantum emitter determines the direction in which it emits, are essential building blocks of non-reciprocal quantum devices, deterministic quantum logical gates and entanglement generation protocols. Yet, a chiral quantum interface that operates at telecom wavelengths, and is compatible with telecommunication infrastructure and silicon photonics, does not yet exist. Here, we report on an integrated chiral quantum interface in the original telecom band (1260-1360 nm), created by interfacing InAs quantum dots with a waveguide-coupled InP microdisk. We tune the quantum dot transitions through the photonic cavity using a strong magnetic field, observing a peak cavity enhancement of 3.3 and an emission directionality of 0.985, demonstrating the near-ideal chiral quantum coupling required for quantum information processing on integrated photonic devices.
summary: The research reports on creating an integrated chiral quantum interface using InAs quantum dots coupled to an InP microdisk waveguide operating in the crucial telecom band. By applying magnetic fields, they demonstrated strong coupling and near-ideal emission directionality ($D=0.985$). This work provides a vital building block for realizing non-reciprocal components needed for advanced quantum logic gates on photonic chips.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a functional, integrated chiral quantum interface operating at telecom wavelengths (1260–1360 nm) necessary for building non-reciprocal quantum devices.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated near-ideal chiral emission directionality ($D=0.985$) in an integrated platform by coupling InAs quantum dots to an InP microdisk waveguide, achieving high performance compatible with silicon photonics.
method: Measurements involve tuning the quantum dot transitions using strong out-of-plane magnetic fields and quantifying directional emission contrast by comparing light collected from left versus right output ports.
model_or_system: The physical system is an integrated chip coupling InAs quantum dots to an InP microdisk waveguide. The physics involves controlling the emitter's spin state via a magnetic field ($B_z$) to induce chiral emission directionality.
key_observables: Chirality/Directionality ($D$), Directional Contrast ($C$), Cavity Enhancement (3.3), and QD lifetime ($	au$).
important_parameters: Telecom wavelength band (1260–1360 nm); Magnetic field strength ($B_z$ up to 8.4 T).
main_assumptions: The derivation of directionality equivalence relies on assumptions about balanced total emission intensity and outcoupling efficiency.
figures_summary: Figures show the integrated platform structure, magnetic field dependence of spectra (showing splitting), lifetime measurements showing resonance enhancement, and plots detailing directional contrast ($C_{\pm}$) vs. $B_z$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents evidence by first establishing the physical setup, then measuring spectral/lifetime changes with $B_z$, quantifying directionality using multiple metrics ($D$ vs $C$), and finally confirming the high performance suitable for quantum protocols.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses hardware requirements for photonic quantum information processing by demonstrating a robust, tunable source of directional single photons at telecom wavelengths.
